A1.justification: Both PDFs describe NarrativeTrack. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across revisions.

before.justification: v2 reports original model evaluations, detection/tracking validation, human quality assessments and diagnostic experiments in the main text and Appendix 9.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds proprietary-model evaluations, a character-salience audit and a conditioned error analysis.

M1.justification: The detection, tracking, contextual recognition, top-four entity selection, CRP and QA-generation procedures remain unchanged. The added selection rationale and human-verification description provide support and documentation rather than establish a revised method.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same 1,006 QA pairs from 406 clips drawn from AVA, Video-MME and LVBench, covering the same reasoning dimensions. The newly disclosed generation-pool size and source breakdown do not establish expanded evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 substantially expands proprietary comparisons beyond GPT-4o by adding Gemini-2.0-Flash, Gemini-2.5-Flash, Gemini-2.5-Pro, Gemini-3-Flash, Gemini-3.1-Pro and GPT-4.1. All thirteen open-source models already appear in v2; changing their stated count from twelve to thirteen corrects the prose.

E3.justification: Section 11.4 introduces model-specific evaluation subsets selected by correct entity-existence predictions. Section 3.1 adds a 100-video audit with spatial-size and occurrence criteria. Existing open-source 20-frame and GPT-4o 20/128-frame settings are retained.

E4.justification: v3 adds targeted checks of whether errors persist after correct entity-existence predictions (Table 10) and whether the top-four clusters capture salient characters. Existing directional, frame-density, distractor, text-only, reversed-video and likelihood analyses remain.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting practices are unchanged, including the three-annotator review and Fleiss' kappa of 0.767. No new repeated-run counts, seeds, uncertainty-estimation procedures or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds detailed results for six models; at 128 frames, Gemini-2.5-Pro leads with 83.80%, while GPT-4o retains 72.27%. All matched v2 Table 2 scores remain unchanged. New Table 10 reports conditioned real/synthetic accuracies of 52.9/58.6 for OGP models versus 41.4/43.7 for OVS models; source-length statistics and salience findings are also added.

T1.justification: The entity-representation definition, detector-fusion and matching equations, recall calculation and likelihood-based scoring formula are unchanged. The added empirical rationale introduces no new formal assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The introduction replaces the claim that GPT-4o achieves the highest accuracy with Gemini-2.5-Pro as the leader. The abstract and conclusion retain the benchmark's novelty, CRP and pipeline contributions, and temporal-perceptual trade-off claims.

C2.justification: Sections 5 and 11.4 newly argue that the observed trade-off persists beyond basic entity-existence errors and qualify interpretation of model-category comparisons. v3 also expands the human-only scope rationale, motivates top-four selection and explains quality-balanced curation from the larger generated pool.

D1.justification: v3 adds a dataset access link, explicitly describes exact-match scoring and human verification of inferred attributes, and discloses the 3.8k generated QA pool and source-duration breakdown. Existing pipeline thresholds, components and appendix prompts are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds distinct LLaVA-NeXT-Video and LLaVA-Video references and removes the LLaVA-OneVision reference previously used for those baselines. Research positioning remains largely unchanged; the expanded Video-MME reference identifies the same work.

P1.justification: v3 moves qualitative results earlier, creates a separate Analysis section and promotes the appendix video-source discussion to its own section. Short explanatory additions, terminology corrections and updated cross-references accompany otherwise largely retained prose.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains six model rows, updated highlighting and a frame-setting caption; Tables 3 and 10 are added. Existing figures and template tables are retained and reflowed, including relocation of the failure examples from Figure 9 to Figure 5.

improvement.justification: The expanded proprietary comparisons provide a broader assessment of model capability, while explicit scoring, curation details and the dataset link improve transparency. The new diagnostic analysis adds useful evidence, but Table 10 compares groups on model-specific subsets and its gaps are described as performance drops, limiting the strength of the interpretation. These limitations temper the otherwise supported gains.
